title: Korean Air 801

route.to_name: Antonio B. Won Pat International Airport

summary: Korean Air Flight 801, a Boeing 747-300 flying from Seoul to Guam, crashed into Bijia Peak on approach to Antonio B. Won Pat International Airport on August 6, 1997, after Captain Park continued a non-precision approach in heavy rain despite the glideslope being out of service. First officer Song and flight engineer Nam noticed the steep descent and said the airport was not in sight, but the captain proceeded until the aircraft struck terrain below the minimum safe altitude, killing 229 of the 254 aboard.
probable_cause: The NTSB cited poor communication between the flight crew as the probable cause, along with the captain's poor decision-making on the non-precision approach.

factors.evidence: The glideslope Instrument Landing System (ILS) for runway 6L was out of service, but Captain Park mistakenly believed it was in service.
Captain Park managed to pick up a signal that was later identified to be from an irrelevant electronic device on the ground.
It was raining heavily in Guam, so visibility was considerably reduced, and the crew attempted an instrument landing.
Despite protests from Nam that the detected signal was not the glide-slope indicator, Park continued the approach.
The aircraft descended below the minimum safe altitude of 1440 ft during its landing approach.
The aircraft crashed into Bijia Peak just short of a VHF omnidirectional range navigation beacon about 3 nmi short of the runway, at an altitude of 660 ft.

events.text: At 1:35 am, Captain Park picked up a signal he believed was the runway 6L glideslope, though the ILS glideslope was actually out of service.
First officer Song and flight engineer Nam noticed the aircraft was descending very steeply and remarked several times that the airport was not in sight.
Flight engineer Nam protested that the detected signal was not the glide-slope indicator, but Captain Park continued the approach.
At 1:42 am the aircraft crashed into Bijia Peak about 3 nmi short of the runway at an altitude of 660 ft, below the 1,440 ft minimum safe altitude.

title: Garuda Indonesia 152
summary: Airbus A300 crashed into mountainous woodlands during approach to Medan after the crew became confused about the correct approach direction. Air traffic control issued conflicting instructions and called the aircraft by the wrong callsign, causing the crew to disregard a critical instruction about approach direction. The crew, unfamiliar with the analog flight instrumentation on the A300B4 FFCC, lost vertical awareness while concentrating on lateral changes and descended below the assigned 2000 foot altitude, striking treetops at 1550 feet.
probable_cause: Confusion regarding approach direction resulted in the crew initiating a left turn instead of a right turn during radar vectoring. This confusion, combined with the crew's focus on lateral changes and inadequate vertical monitoring, caused descent below assigned altitude. Contributing factors included poor ATC vectoring, inadequate conversion training for pilots switching between A300 models with different instrumentation, and failure of the GPWS system.

factors.evidence: ATC initially issued instruction using wrong callsign causing crew to disregard instruction about approach direction from south side of runway.
Crew believed they were flying approach on north side of airport per approach chart, but ATC intended south side approach.
Crew's vertical awareness reduced while concentrating on aircraft's lateral changes during confused approach.
First officer distracted during turn and did not notice aircraft turning left when right turn was expected.
GPWS system failed for undetermined reasons and did not provide ground proximity warning.
Aircraft struck treetops at 1550 feet above mean sea level in mountainous woodlands.

events.text: Medan ATC clears Flight 152 for ILS approach to runway 5 from 316 degree heading, instructs crew to turn left to 240 degrees to intercept ILS localizer.
ATC instructs crew to turn further left to 215 degrees for continued vectoring.
Medan ATC instructs crew to descend to 2000 feet and turn right heading 046 degrees to line up for runway 05, but controller confused about aircraft identity with another Flight 152 in area.
ATC initially uses wrong callsign Merpati 152, crew disregards instruction, ATC then queries with correct callsign Indonesia 152 but fails to repeat that approach would be on south side of runway.
Crew believes they are flying approach on north side of airport per approach chart, captain initiates left turn to 046 heading instead of right turn as instructed.
First officer distracted during turn, does not notice aircraft turning left for a while when right turn was expected.
Aircraft descends below assigned 2000 foot altitude while crew concentrating on lateral changes and losing vertical awareness.
Aircraft strikes treetops at 1550 feet above mean sea level in mountainous woodlands near Buah Nabar, GPWS system fails and provides no warning.

title: Aerosvit 241
summary: The aircraft entered Greek airspace and the crew mistook an ATC message intended for another aircraft. During the approach to Thessaloniki, the crew became disoriented and lost, failing to follow the proper approach route. Despite numerous cues from ATC and multiple opportunities to declare an emergency, the confused crew refused to declare emergency and attempted to re-orient themselves. The aircraft crashed into a mountainside during the second approach.
probable_cause: The flight crew's navigational error caused the crew to become disoriented and lost during the second approach to Thessaloniki. The crew failed to follow the route that they were supposed to take and did not declare emergency despite being in a difficult situation.

factors.evidence: The crew immediately contacted Thessaloniki Approach and mistook a message for an Olympic Airways flight, thinking the descent instruction was for them
The aircraft somehow arrived in Thessaloniki at a very high altitude and continued to pass over the airport, heading south; the controller noticed this and informed the crew

During the second approach, the controller repeatedly asked about their position for confirmation; the crew didn't report any problems regarding the approach procedure but suddenly requested a radar vector
The crew stated they were on the right track when based on ATC information they should have been north of the airport
The crew failed to follow the route that they were supposed to take and the aircraft ultimately crashed onto the mountains
Despite numerous cues, the confused crew refused to declare emergency over the situation
The aircraft was designed with Eastern European navigation system different from Western systems; there was no evidence that required modifications had been conducted for VOR-DME-ILS approach
The aircraft flew into a mountainside during the missed approach

events.text: Flight 241 entered Greek airspace and immediately contacted Thessaloniki Approach; the crew mistook a descent message intended for an Olympic Airways flight
The aircraft arrived at a very high altitude and continued to pass over the airport, heading south; the controller noticed and informed the crew they were off course
The crew was instructed to climb to 6000 feet and maintain position in the south holding pattern, then instructed to turn back to the airport's VOR
During the second approach, the controller repeatedly asked about their position; the crew stated they were on the right track and should have been north of the airport
The crew suddenly requested a radar vector to the controller; since Thessaloniki had no radar, the controller refused and asked the crew to comply with the written procedure
The aircraft flew into a mountainside during the second approach while attempting to re-orient themselves

title: SilkAir 185
summary: SilkAir Flight 185 departed Jakarta at 15:37 local time for an 80-minute flight to Singapore. At 16:05, the cockpit voice recorder ceased recording after Captain Tsu stated he was leaving the cockpit to fetch water. The flight data recorder also stopped recording at 16:11. Flight 185 remained level at FL350 until it started a rapid and nearly vertical dive around 16:12. Parts of the aircraft separated from the fuselage due to high forces from the nearly supersonic dive, and the aircraft hit the Musi River, killing all 104 people on board.
probable_cause: The NTSC concluded that the evidence was insufficient to determine a cause. The NTSB concluded that the crash was the result of deliberate flight-control inputs, most likely by the captain. Investigators found that flight inputs had moved the horizontal stabilizer from level flight to a full nose-down descent.

factors.evidence: Investigators found that flight inputs from one of the pilots had moved the stabilizer from level flight to a full nose-down descent.
It is likely that Captain Tsu pulled out the CVR circuit breaker while exiting the cockpit.
The FDR stopped recording at 16:11, and if Captain Tsu was responsible for the crash, he must have devised some excuse to persuade the first officer to leave the flight deck.
The aircraft started a rapid and nearly vertical dive, and parts of the aircraft separated from the fuselage due to high forces from the nearly supersonic dive.

events.text: The Boeing 737 departed Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport's runway 25R for an 80-minute flight to Singapore's Changi Airport.
The cockpit voice recorder ceased recording after Captain Tsu stated he was leaving the cockpit to fetch water.
The flight data recorder stopped recording.
The aircraft started a rapid and nearly vertical dive around 16:12.
The aircraft hit the Musi River near Palembang, Sumatra, and was travelling faster than the speed of sound.
